title: President's Scholarship
legacy_titles: Presidential Scholars Program (University of Nebraska System umbrella programme)
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded automatically at admission to new first-time freshmen; full cost of attendance benefit
funding_type: Full cost of attendance plus annual stipend (state public tuition benefit funded through the University of Nebraska and donor support)
administering_authority: University of Nebraska System (Presidential Scholars Program), administered at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln by the Office of Scholarships & Financial Aid
implementing_agency: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Office of Scholarships & Financial Aid (Husker Hub) and the Undergraduate Office of Admissions; formal award acceptance is processed through the University of Nebraska System
programme_action: University of Nebraska Presidential Scholars Program (state tuition-benefit programme announced February 2024 by the Board of Regents and expanded November 2024)
description: The President's Scholarship is the University of Nebraska-Lincoln's award for incoming Nebraska residents with near-perfect ACT or SAT scores, offered under the University of Nebraska System's Presidential Scholars Program. It covers the full cost of attendance at the University of Nebraska for up to four years (eight semesters, or completion of a bachelor's degree), with three inclusive summers, plus an annual US$5,000 stipend. Cost of attendance is the university's standard budget: full tuition and required fees plus the standard budgeted amount for housing and meals, books and supplies, transportation and personal expenses. It is a renewable, automatic-consideration scholarship: eligible applicants are considered on the UNL application for admission without a separate scholarship form.

programme_structure.award_types: Single highest-value incoming first-year award; umbrella programme is the University of Nebraska System Presidential Scholars Program, usable at any University of Nebraska campus
programme_structure.award_types_detail: One award type at UNL: full cost of attendance plus annual stipend. The scholarship may transfer to the University of Nebraska at Kearney (UNK), University of Nebraska at Omaha (UNO), University of Nebraska Medical Center (UNMC) or the Nebraska College of Technical Agriculture (NCTA). Lower UNL first-year awards include the Chancellor's Tuition Scholarship (up to $8,000/year) and the Regents Scholar Tuition Commitment.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Renewal is dependent on maintaining a cumulative GPA of 3.500 (the University computes GPAs to three decimal places and does not round), completing at least 24 UNL credits each academic year (fall/spring; repeated courses count only once), enrolling full-time (at least 12 UNL credit hours) in each fall and spring semester with hours officially registered by the sixth day of classes (census date), and maintaining continuous enrolment in each consecutive fall/spring semester. Renewal determinations are made at the end of each spring semester. Renewable for a maximum of eight consecutive semesters.
programme_structure.intake: Fall entry (with a Spring option for new first-year students; the official guideline pages are labeled 'For New First Year Students in Fall [year] (and Spring [year+1])')

status_label: Open for the currently recruiting entry (priority deadline 1 November 2026)
status_note: The award is open for the next entry cycle. UNL's Fall 2027 first-year application opened 1 August 2026, with a 1 November 2026 priority application deadline and a 1 February 2027 final deadline; scholarship offers for applicants who applied by 1 November are released 11 February. The researched source page 'President's Scholarship for 2026-2027' covers new first-year students entering Fall 2026/Spring 2027, whose admission deadlines fell in November 2025 / February 2026 and have now passed; UNL publishes a parallel 'President's Scholarship for 2027-2028' page with identical award terms and renewal conditions. Next cycle expected: Fall 2028 entry, with the same recurring 1 November priority and 1 February final deadlines.
verification_notes: Verified against ten official unl.edu / nebraska.edu pages. Award value, cost-of-attendance components, renewal criteria, eligibility and the Nebraska-resident restriction were confirmed on financialaid.unl.edu/presidents-scholarship-2026-2027/ and on admissions.unl.edu/cost/scholarships/presidents-scholarship/. Automatic consideration and the November 1 / February 1 priority and final deadlines were confirmed on the admissions award page and admissions.unl.edu/apply/first-year-dates-deadlines/. Cost-of-attendance component definitions and the 2026-2027 standard COA figures were confirmed on financialaid.unl.edu/cost/estimated-cost-attendance/2026-2027/. International-student ineligibility is confirmed by (a) the awards page tagging the President's Scholarship as 'First-Year, In-State' only, (b) the UNL Scholarship Guidelines page listing it only under 'First-Year Nebraska Residents' and providing separate Global Excellence, Global Laureate, Global Ambassador and Global Delegate Tuition Scholarships for first-year international students, and (c) the statutory note on the admissions award page. The exact published deadline for the formal Statement of Acceptance with the University of Nebraska System is NOT published on any public page reached: UNL states only that recipients must formally accept or decline the award through the University of Nebraska System 'by the published deadline' and that 'Detailed instructions for completing this process will be provided directly to recipients.' This remains an unverified item.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Application for admission opens 1 August for the following fall; priority application deadline 1 November; final in-state admission-materials deadline 1 February; offers released 11 February; final official test scores due 1 May
application_deadline.application_period: Fall 2027 entry: application open from 1 August 2026; priority deadline 1 November 2026; final deadline 1 February 2027
application_deadline.official_rule: UNL publishes two dates for this award: a priority deadline of 1 November to submit the application for admission (applicants are notified of scholarship awards on 11 February), and a final deadline of 1 February. UNL's First-Year Dates & Deadlines page specifies that for the Fall 2027 cycle, 1 February 2027 is the deadline by which in-state students must submit all admission application materials to be considered for academic scholarships, that applications after 1 November 2026 are reviewed on a rolling basis with rolling notifications from 25 February 2027, and that final official ACT/SAT scores from the February test date or earlier are due by 1 May 2027.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Missing the 1 November priority deadline does not disqualify an applicant; UNL states rolling scholarship notifications and updates begin on 25 February 2027 for admitted students who applied for admission after 1 November. However, applicants who apply after 1 November receive awards later and on a space-available basis, and all admission application materials must still be submitted by the final 1 February date for scholarship consideration. Dates are subject to change per UNL.

programme_duration.official_range: Up to four years (eight semesters), or completion of a bachelor's degree, with three inclusive summers
programme_duration.renewal_note: Renewable for a maximum of eight consecutive semesters subject to annual renewal criteria. Renewal requires a 3.500 cumulative GPA (computed to three decimal places, unrounded), completion of at least 24 UNL credits each academic year (fall/spring; repeated courses count once), full-time enrolment of at least 12 UNL credits in each fall and spring semester registered by the sixth day of classes, and continuous enrolment in each consecutive fall/spring semester. Summer enrolment is optional; renewal determinations are made at the end of each spring semester.

funding.scholarship_type: Full cost of attendance (institutional/state public tuition benefit) plus annual stipend
funding.monthly_amount_note: The award is not paid as a monthly allowance. The stipend component is an annual US$5,000 amount. No official source publishes a monthly payment schedule.
funding.travel_amount_note: No separate travel amount is published. Transportation is one of the cost-of-attendance components the award covers at the standard budgeted amount (the 2026-2027 UNL standard COA for an on/off-campus resident lists Personal Expenses of $2,324, which the COA notes include transportation, clothing and other miscellaneous personal costs).
funding.fully_funded_note: Covered at the standard cost of attendance: full tuition and required fees plus the standard budgeted amount for housing and meals, books and supplies, transportation and personal expenses, for up to four years/eight semesters with three inclusive summers, plus an annual US$5,000 stipend. Not an unconditional cash award: it is capped at the standard budgeted COA, cannot be combined with other federal, state or University tuition waivers, is discontinued on withdrawal or non-registration, and does not cover penalty fees, programme/travel fees for global experience programmes, or non-credit courses.

tuition.note: Full tuition and required fees are covered at the standard budgeted rate. UNL's 2026-2027 estimated cost of attendance for a resident undergraduate living on or off campus lists Tuition & Fees of $11,472 (non-resident $31,542).
tuition.conditions: Covers full tuition and required fees, including mandatory student service fees, laboratory fees related to particular courses, and miscellaneous fees such as online course fees, registration fees and technology fees. Does not cover penalty fees (late fees, damage fees, parking citations), differential programme tuition, or non-credit and non-term-specific correspondence courses.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source; the stipend is annual, not monthly

annual_stipend.note: The official award terms state the award covers full cost of attendance 'plus an annual $5,000' and the University of Nebraska System describes this as a '$5,000 annual stipend'. The basis is a flat annual amount paid in addition to the cost-of-attendance coverage; no official page publishes a calculation method or per-credit/per-semester derivation.
annual_stipend.conditions: No additional stipend is paid during the summer. The US$5,000 figure is confirmed on financialaid.unl.edu/presidents-scholarship-2026-2027/, financialaid.unl.edu/presidents-scholarship-2027-2028/, admissions.unl.edu/cost/scholarships/presidents-scholarship/ and nebraska.edu/presidential-scholars.

travel_allowance.note: No separate travel allowance is published; transportation is covered only within the standard budgeted personal-expense component of the cost of attendance

visa_support.note: Not published in official source; the award is not open to international students, so no visa support is offered

book_allowance.note: Books and supplies are covered at the standard budgeted amount. UNL's 2026-2027 estimated cost of attendance lists Books & Supplies of $1,128 for a resident undergraduate living on or off campus.
book_allowance.conditions: Covered as part of the standard cost of attendance rather than as a separate itemised allowance.

accommodation_support.note: Housing and meals are covered at the standard budgeted amount. UNL's 2026-2027 estimated cost of attendance lists Housing & Food of $13,950 for a resident undergraduate living on or off campus, and $6,000 for a student living at home with a parent or guardian.
accommodation_support.conditions: Covered at the standard budgeted amount, not at actual housing charges. First-year students enrolled for six or more credit hours must live in approved on-campus housing unless they meet the on-campus residency requirement; students who enroll but do not meet it are charged for an unassigned traditional double room.

bond.note: No service bond or repayment obligation is published. There is a donor-relations condition instead: because the programme is supported through the generosity of donors, recipients may be asked to consent to participate in university events and promotions as a condition of accepting the scholarship.

total_estimated_value.note: Not published in official source and deliberately not computed. UNL's standard 2026-2027 resident cost of attendance for an undergraduate living on or off campus is $28,938; adding the $5,000 annual stipend to a capped COA figure would not be a published award value and is not presented as one.

eligible_applicants: Graduating high school seniors who are first-time freshmen
United States citizens, or qualified aliens verified as lawfully present in the United States under Nebraska State Statutes 4-111 and 4-112
Applicants who apply and are accepted to a University of Nebraska campus and enrol full-time
final_year_condition: This is the entry-level qualification rule for a bachelor's-entry award: the scholarship is for graduating high school seniors (first-time freshmen) entering a bachelor's degree. A 'final year' bachelor's-student scenario does not apply.
equivalent_degree_note: No published provision for an equivalent secondary-education completion route (such as GED, home-school completion or an international qualification) was found on the official pages reviewed. UNL publishes a first-year admission requirement of 4 units of English coursework and other specified core-course units; any deficiency must be removed before enrolment. International qualifications are not relevant because the award requires Nebraska residency and US citizenship or verified lawful presence.
nationality_quota: Restricted to United States citizens, or qualified aliens verified as lawfully present in the United States (Nebraska State Statutes 4-110, 4-111 and 4-112), and restricted additionally to Nebraska residents; no numerical quota is published

eligibility.citizenship: Must be a United States citizen, or a qualified alien verified as lawfully present in the United States (Nebraska State Statutes 4-111 and 4-112). International (non-US) students are not eligible; UNL lists this award under 'First-Year Nebraska Residents' and offers separate Global Excellence, Global Laureate, Global Ambassador and Global Delegate Tuition Scholarships to first-year international students.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Must be a Nebraska resident. UNL classifies the President's Scholarship as 'First-Year, In-State' only.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Must be a graduating high school senior and a first-time freshman.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Composite ACT score of 36, or SAT total of 1570-1600. For the enhanced ACT introduced in September 2025, the optional Science test must be taken and a 36 STEM Score (average of the math and science sections) achieved. From the February test date or earlier, final official test scores are due by 1 May. Self-reported scores are not considered and superscores are not considered.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: 3.500 cumulative GPA for renewal (computed to three decimal places, not rounded). No minimum entering high-school GPA is published for the award itself.
eligibility.language_requirement: No English-language test requirement is published for this award. UNL's published first-year admission requirement is 4 units of English coursework, all units including intensive reading and writing experience.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Cannot be combined with any other tuition waiver from federal, state or University sources (for example the Employee Dependent Waiver).
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: First-time freshman; must apply and be accepted at a University of Nebraska campus and enrol full-time (at least 12 UNL credit hours) each fall and spring semester.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No percentage or grade-class-rank threshold is published for this award.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Composite ACT of 36, or SAT total of 1570-1600, inclusive of the science section. For the enhanced ACT available to all testers from September 2025, students must elect the optional science portion and also achieve a 36 STEM Score (average of the math and science section). Official (not self-reported) scores must be submitted to the campus; superscores are not considered. UNL states that for students matriculating in Fall 2027 the qualifying routes are a composite 36 on exams taken before the Science component was used to calculate a STEM score, or a composite 36 and a STEM score of 36 on exams where a STEM score is calculated, or an SAT equivalent of 1570-1600.
selection_factors_may_include: Official ACT or SAT score meeting the qualifying threshold
Admission to a University of Nebraska campus

english_requirement.test_score_note: No English-language proficiency test score is published as a requirement of the President's Scholarship. UNL's published first-year admission requirement relevant to English is 4 units of English coursework, all units including intensive reading and writing experience. UNL's International Dates & Deadlines and international student admissions pages govern English proficiency for international applicants, who are not eligible for this award.

language_of_instruction.language_note: Undergraduate instruction at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln is in English. The award does not restrict programme or language of instruction; the published cost-of-attendance and renewal terms apply to all UNL bachelor's programmes.

application_method.application_route: Apply for undergraduate admission directly to the University of Nebraska-Lincoln. Eligible applicants are automatically considered for the President's Scholarship on the basis of their UNL admission application and official ACT/SAT scores; no separate scholarship application form is required for this award. Filing the FAFSA is encouraged by 1 February for a comprehensive aid offer but is not the scholarship application.
application_steps: Submit official ACT or SAT scores to UNL Admissions (self-reported and superscored scores are not considered).
Apply for UNL undergraduate admission by 1 November for priority scholarship consideration (application opens 1 August for the following fall).
Confirm Nebraska residency as part of the admission application.
Optionally file the FAFSA by 1 February to receive a comprehensive scholarship and financial aid offer.
Receive the scholarship offer in MyRED ('Financial Aid' tab) on 11 February if you applied by 1 November.
Formally accept or decline the award through the University of Nebraska System by the published deadline; detailed instructions are provided directly to recipients.
Pay or defer the enrollment deposit by 1 May and enrol full-time (at least 12 UNL credit hours) each fall and spring semester.
application_method.application_fee: UNL publishes an undergraduate application fee; the fee is not waived by this award and no fee exemption for the scholarship is published.

universal_documents: University of Nebraska-Lincoln undergraduate application for admission
Official ACT or SAT score report sent to UNL Admissions
commonly_requested_documents: High school transcript or equivalent showing completion of required core-course units
Proof of Nebraska residency as part of the admission application
FAFSA Form (encouraged by 1 February, required only for a comprehensive financial aid offer, not for this award)
official_application_documents.secondary_school_documents: High school coursework in required core units, including 4 units of English (all units including intensive reading and writing experience), 4 units of Mathematics, Natural Sciences and other core requirements published by UNL Admissions. No separate scholarship-specific secondary-school document package is published for this award.

academic_documents.item: Official ACT or SAT score report submitted to UNL Admissions
academic_documents.note: Self-reported scores are not considered and superscores are not considered. For the enhanced ACT the optional Science test must be taken and a 36 STEM Score achieved.

financial_documents.note: Encouraged by 1 February so that the scholarship offer released on 11 February includes financial aid; not required to be considered for the President's Scholarship itself.

additional_documents.note: Submitted as part of the UNL application for admission; the award is classified as First-Year, In-State.

additional_documents.item: Statement of Acceptance with the University of Nebraska System
additional_documents.note: Required only after an award is offered. Recipients must formally accept or decline through the University of Nebraska System by the published deadline; the exact deadline is not published publicly and instructions are sent directly to recipients.

required_documents: University of Nebraska-Lincoln undergraduate application for admission
Official ACT or SAT score report sent to UNL Admissions
FAFSA Form (optional for this award; required by 1 February to receive a comprehensive aid offer)
Statement of Acceptance with the University of Nebraska System (post-offer, required to accept the award)

selection_process.decision_maker: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Office of Scholarships & Financial Aid (Husker Hub) with the Undergraduate Office of Admissions, under the University of Nebraska System Presidential Scholars Program
selection_process.selection_type: Automatic consideration on admission based on a published test-score threshold; no separate application, essay or interview
possible_stages: Apply and be admitted to the University of Nebraska-Lincoln
Official ACT or SAT score verification against the qualifying threshold
Nebraska residency and first-time freshman status verification
Scholarship offer issued in MyRED on 11 February (priority applicants) or on a rolling basis from 25 February (late applicants)
Formal accept/decline through the University of Nebraska System by the published deadline
Annual renewal determination at the end of each spring semester
selection_process.weighting_note: UNL publishes no weighting or rubric. Consideration is automatic for applicants who meet the published test-score threshold, with no separate application, essay, interview or committee scoring published.
selection_process.results_timing: Scholarship award offers are available in MyRED on 11 February for admitted students who applied by 1 November; rolling scholarship notifications and updates begin on 25 February for admitted students who applied after 1 November.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: This is UNL's highest-value incoming first-year academic scholarship. UNL's other first-year awards are worth less (for example the Chancellor's Tuition Scholarship at up to $8,000/year) and are typically offered to applicants with lower test scores.

selection_criteria.additional_factors: Nebraska residency; first-time freshman status; admission to a University of Nebraska campus; official verified ACT/SAT score meeting the qualifying threshold

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (or another University of Nebraska System campus if the award is transferred)
possible_awards: Bachelor's degree at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln

Bachelor's degree at the University of Nebraska at Omaha, University of Nebraska at Kearney, University of Nebraska Medical Center or the Nebraska College of Technical Agriculture if the President's Scholarship transfers
degree_outcome.degree_note: The award supports completion of a bachelor's degree in up to four years or eight semesters, whichever comes first. To complete a degree in eight semesters a student must earn an average of 15 credit hours each semester.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: The award cannot be applied toward course credit that will be transferred from another institution. For global experience programmes the commitment may be applied toward UNL course credit where university tuition is charged; programme and/or travel fees are not covered.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Full tuition and required fees are covered for up to four years (eight semesters) or completion of a bachelor's degree, with three inclusive summers, at the standard budgeted cost of attendance.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No application-fee waiver is published for recipients of this scholarship.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Recipients must formally accept or decline the award through the University of Nebraska System by the published deadline, and should refer to the formal scholarship Statement of Acceptance with the University of Nebraska System for complete terms and conditions. Because the programme is supported through the generosity of donors, recipients may be asked to consent to participate in university events and promotions as a condition of accepting the scholarship.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Covered as part of the standard cost of attendance: full tuition and required fees, standard budgeted housing and meals, books and supplies, transportation and personal expenses. Mandatory student service fees, laboratory fees related to particular courses, and miscellaneous fees such as online course fees, registration fees and technology fees are covered. An amount equal to the semester tuition and fee charges is credited to the recipient's student account, and any award exceeding total institutional charges for a semester is refunded by the Office of Student Accounts (direct deposit encouraged).

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm first-time freshman status (not a transfer student)
Sit the ACT including the optional Science section (or the SAT) and achieve a composite 36 or SAT 1570-1600
Send official scores to UNL Admissions early; self-reported and superscored scores are not considered
Apply for admission by 1 November for priority consideration
Complete the high-school core-course requirements, including 4 units of English
File the FAFSA by 1 February if you want a comprehensive aid offer with the scholarship
Watch MyRED for the 11 February offer and follow the University of Nebraska System acceptance instructions

programme_comparison_fields.award_value: Full cost of attendance plus US$5,000/year
programme_comparison_fields.duration: Up to 4 years / 8 semesters plus 3 inclusive summers
programme_comparison_fields.renewal: 3.500 cumulative GPA and 24 UNL credits per year, full-time each fall/spring
programme_comparison_fields.eligibility: Nebraska residents, US citizens or lawfully present qualified aliens, first-time freshmen with ACT 36 or SAT 1570-1600
programme_comparison_fields.application: Automatic consideration on the UNL admission application; no separate form

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: No essay or motivation letter is required or considered for this award; selection is automatic on the published test-score threshold and Nebraska residency. Effort is better spent on the UNL application, on official score submission and on meeting core-course requirements.
profile_fit_labels: US citizen or lawfully present qualified alien
Seeking a full-ride total cost of attendance award
common_mistakes: Assuming international students are eligible: UNL restricts this award to Nebraska residents who are US citizens or lawfully present qualified aliens, and offers separate Global scholarships to international students
Relying on self-reported or superscored ACT/SAT results: official scores are required and superscores are not considered
Sitting the enhanced ACT without the optional Science section, which is mandatory under the current qualifying rules
Missing the 1 November priority deadline and expecting an offer with the 11 February round
Failing to formally accept the award through the University of Nebraska System by the published deadline
Dropping below 12 UNL credit hours in a fall or spring semester, or falling short of 24 UNL credits over the academic year
Assuming summer funding is automatic: summer use requires meeting renewal criteria and filing the Summer Aid Application in MyRED, and no stipend is paid in summer
Expecting actual rather than standard budgeted costs to be covered: penalty fees, programme and travel fees are excluded

risk_flags.risk: Extremely narrow eligibility: Nebraska residency plus a composite ACT of 36 or SAT 1570-1600
risk_flags.impact: Only a very small number of Nebraska high-school seniors each year will qualify, so most applicants will not receive this award
risk_flags.mitigation: Verify residency and current score thresholds on the official pages before investing effort; also review UNL's Chancellor's Tuition Scholarship and Regents Scholar Tuition Commitment

risk_flags.impact: Non-US applicants and non-Nebraska residents are excluded, and the award cannot be used as a US study funding route
risk_flags.mitigation: International applicants should instead review UNL's Global Excellence, Global Laureate, Global Ambassador and Global Delegate Tuition Scholarships

risk_flags.impact: Falling below a 3.500 cumulative GPA, below 12 UNL credit hours in any fall or spring semester, or below 24 UNL credits over an academic year ends or reduces the benefit; repeated courses count only once
risk_flags.mitigation: Plan a 15-credit-per-semester schedule, avoid repeated courses, and register at least 12 credits by the sixth day of classes each semester

risk_flags.risk: The published 32-35 ACT pathway is no longer available for incoming Fall 2026 students due to budget constraints
risk_flags.impact: Applicants with strong but not perfect scores who might have qualified under earlier rules are now outside the qualifying range
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm the current-cycle qualifying routes on the award page and the University of Nebraska System Presidential Scholars page before applying

risk_flags.risk: Coverage is capped at the standard budgeted cost of attendance
risk_flags.impact: Differential programme tuition (for example in Business, Architecture and Engineering), penalty fees, programme and travel fees, and costs above the standard budget are not covered
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget separately for differential tuition, parking, damage and late fees, and global-experience programme fees

risk_flags.risk: Award terms change annually for new incoming students
risk_flags.impact: UNL warns that scholarships are subject to change each year for new incoming students, so the current cycle's value or criteria may differ
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-check the cycle-specific guideline page (2026-2027 or 2027-2028) and the System programme page each admissions cycle

risk_flags.risk: The formal Statement of Acceptance deadline is not publicly published
risk_flags.impact: Recipients who miss the acceptance deadline reported directly to them could forfeit the award without a publicly verifiable fallback date
risk_flags.mitigation: Monitor MyRED and the email address used on the admission application after the 11 February offer release, and accept promptly

risk_flags.impact: The commitment is discontinued if the recipient withdraws from school or fails to register for consecutive semesters, unless a scholarship leave of absence is granted for extenuating circumstances
risk_flags.mitigation: Maintain continuous enrolment in consecutive fall/spring semesters and request a leave-of-absence exception before withdrawing

application_status_workflow: Applied for admission to UNL with official ACT/SAT scores submitted
Formally accepted through the University of Nebraska System
Enrolled full-time and scholarship credited to the student account
Renewal determination at the end of each spring semester
Award completed (eight semesters or bachelor's degree completed)
best_fit: A graduating US high-school senior who is a Nebraska resident and a US citizen or lawfully present qualified alien with an official composite ACT score of 36 (or SAT total of 1570-1600, including the enhanced-ACT Science route and 36 STEM score), applying as a first-time freshman to the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, who wants their entire budgeted cost of attendance plus a US$5,000 annual stipend covered for four years.
not_best_fit: International students and applicants who are not US citizens or verified lawfully present qualified aliens
Students who are not Nebraska residents (out-of-state and domestic non-Nebraska applicants)
Transfer students, current undergraduates and applicants who already hold a bachelor's degree
Applicants whose official ACT score is below 36 or SAT score below 1570-1600
Applicants who cannot commit to full-time enrolment of at least 12 UNL credits every fall and spring semester and 24 UNL credits per academic year
Applicants seeking a scholarship that can be combined with another tuition waiver
Applicants who need funding for a master's degree or for non-credit study

image.logo_verification_method: Fetched the official University of Nebraska-Lincoln homepage at https://www.unl.edu/ and read its <link rel="icon"> declarations. The referenced SVG asset at https://wdn-cdn.unl.edu/wdn/templates_6.1/includes/global/favicon/icon.svg was then fetched directly and returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/svg+xml; the file is the University of Nebraska-Lincoln 'N' mark in scarlet (#d00) and white, matching the header logo SVG used on unl.edu pages. A PNG apple-touch-icon version is also published on the same official UNL domain at https://wdn-cdn.unl.edu/wdn/templates_6.1/includes/global/favicon/apple-touch-icon.png (HTTP 200, image/png). The asset is served from the official unl.edu domain and is the awarding university's own mark, so it satisfies the logo sourcing rules.
image.image_usage_note: Logo asset located on the official unl.edu domain and verified as reachable. No photographic image was sourced, since no verified official campus photo specific to this award was identified.

A third-party aggregator page (collegereadyparent.org) stated that renewal requires '30 credit hours each academic year' for incoming Fall 2026 students; this contradicts the official 24-credit requirement and was rejected in favour of the official financialaid.unl.edu pages.

database_notes: The official award name is 'President's Scholarship'. The umbrella University of Nebraska System programme is the 'Presidential Scholars Program'; UNL's Scholarship Guidelines index lists it as 'Presidential Scholarship'. Both are recorded in legacy_titles. No acronym or widely used short form exists, so short_title repeats the official award name.

Cycle note: the assigned source page is the 2026-2027 guideline page for new first-year students in Fall 2026 and Spring 2027. UNL also publishes a 2027-2028 guideline page with identical award terms and renewal conditions. Because UNL's first-year admissions cycle has already rolled over to Fall 2027 (application opened 1 August 2026), the record reports the currently open Fall 2027 deadlines (priority 1 November 2026, final 1 February 2027, offers 11 February 2027) while citing the 2026-2027 page as the deepest verified official page for this award.

International students are NOT eligible for this award. This was verified three ways on official pages: the admissions award page tags it 'First-Year, In-State'; UNL's Scholarship Guidelines page lists it only under 'First-Year Nebraska Residents' and provides separate Global Excellence, Global Laureate, Global Ambassador and Global Delegate Tuition Scholarships for first-year international students; and the award page carries the statutory restriction (Neb. Rev. Stat. 4-110, 4-111, 4-112) requiring US citizenship or verified lawful presence as a qualified alien.

The US$5,000 figure is officially described as an annual amount added to full cost-of-attendance coverage ('plus an annual $5,000'; the System programme describes it as a '$5,000 annual stipend'). No official page publishes a calculation method, per-credit rate or monthly payment schedule, so monthly_amount is null and total_estimated_value is deliberately not computed.

Cost-of-attendance figures quoted are UNL's published 2026-2027 estimated COA for a resident undergraduate living on or off campus: Tuition & Fees $11,472; Housing & Food $13,950; Books & Supplies $1,128; Personal Expenses $2,324; Loan Fees $64 (if applicable); Total $28,938. The $2,324 Personal Expenses line is described by UNL as including transportation, clothing and other miscellaneous personal costs, so transportation is covered within it rather than as a separate published amount. A living-at-home variant totals $20,988.

No English-language test requirement is published for this award; UNL's published first-year admission requirement is 4 units of English coursework including intensive reading and writing experience. All english_requirement score fields are therefore null and universal_requirement is false.
age_limit is null and gender_restriction is false because no age or gender condition is published for this award. No age cap has been invented.
bachelor_requirement is false and final_year_bachelor_allowed is false because this award funds entry into a bachelor's degree and requires high-school completion, not a completed bachelor's.
equivalent_degree_allowed is false because no official page publishes an equivalent secondary-education completion route (GED, home-school or international qualification) for this award.

No service bond or repayment obligation is published; a donor-relations consent condition is recorded instead because UNL states recipients may be asked to consent to participate in university events and promotions as a condition of accepting the scholarship.

document_checklist.identity_documents, language_documents and recommendation_documents are empty and application_essays is empty because the official pages publish no essay, recommendation-letter or language-document requirement for this automatic consideration award. Empty arrays are used rather than invented entries.

official_application_documents fields for document_language, document_format, transcript_requirement, certified_translation_requirement and two_recommendation_letters are null because the official pages do not publish such specifications for this award.
source_last_updated is null because the financialaid.unl.edu pages reviewed carry no visible 'last updated' date.

logo_url is an official University of Nebraska-Lincoln favicon/icon asset served on the official unl.edu domain (wdn-cdn.unl.edu), verified as HTTP 200 with the correct image Content-Type and visually matching the UNL header 'N' mark. No third-party or aggregator logo source was used.

A third-party aggregator claim that renewal requires 30 credits per academic year for incoming Fall 2026 students was found and rejected as contradicting the official financialaid.unl.edu pages, which state 24 UNL credits per academic year.
